name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.not_finiteDimensional
title: The completed CAR algebra is infinite-dimensional

content.assumptions: The algebra $A$ is the fixed completed CAR algebra. For every $n\geq0$, its canonical stage map $\iota_n:A_n\to A$ is complex-linear and injective, and $\dim_{\mathbb C}A_n=(2^n)^2$. These are established properties of this construction, not new assumptions on an arbitrary algebra.
content.conclusion: No finite integer can be the complex dimension of $A$: every stage contributes an embedded vector space of dimension $4^n$, and these dimensions are unbounded.
content.display_title: The completed CAR algebra is infinite-dimensional
content.lean_realization_notes: The conclusion concerns vector-space dimension over $\mathbb C$. It does not require an irreducible representation or a claim about compact operators.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the norm completion of the matrix system $A_n=M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ with embeddings $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$. Then $A$ is not finite-dimensional as a complex vector space.
content.one_sentence_role: Rules out finite dimension by retaining matrix subalgebras of unbounded dimension.

proof_steps.text: Assume that $A$ is finite-dimensional and write $k=\dim_{\mathbb C}A$.
The linear injection $\iota_{k+1}$ forces $\dim_{\mathbb C}A_{k+1}\leq k$.
The stage dimension is $(2^{k+1})^2>k$, yielding the contradiction.

content.proof_summary: If $A$ had finite dimension $k$, injectivity of each $\iota_n$ would give $(2^n)^2\leq k$. Take $n=k+1$. The elementary inequality $k<2^n\leq(2^n)^2$ contradicts that bound.
